title: How a Motorcycle Responds to Your Controls

slides.title: Engine Braking
slides.objective: Explain why closing the throttle can slow the motorcycle.
slides.headline: Low gears make engine braking feel stronger.
slides.visual_description: A simple flow from a closed throttle through drivetrain resistance to rear-wheel deceleration.

beats.summary: Closing the throttle lets the moving motorcycle turn the engine through the drivetrain, and a lower gear makes that resistance feel stronger.
beats.narration_guidance: Connect the stronger low-gear sensation to the gear ratio without implying that the wheel brakes are applied.

deep_dive.explanation: At the same road speed, a lower gear makes the engine turn faster. When the throttle is closed, that ratio couples more engine resistance back to the rear wheel, so the slowing effect feels stronger.
caveats: Available tyre grip still limits deceleration.
An abrupt downshift can unsettle the rear wheel.
